statement: By the time a03 ran, crates/enforcer-domain/src/ids.rs (not the workpack's named rule_id.rs) already defined RuleId as a fully-formed branded newtype via a shared `branded_string!` macro: private inner field, TryFrom<String>/FromStr parse-at-boundary constructor, serde try_from/into wiring, Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq/Hash/PartialOrd/Ord derive, ts_rs::TS, Display, and a fail-closed grammar validator (uppercase-alnum prefix + dash-separated alnum/dot segments, e.g. RR-6.1). The same ids.rs module also houses HubName/LaneId/CorrelationId/CausationId/ThreatId (the a04/a05/a06 sibling newtypes), consistent with a04's memory record about the workspace converging on one shared ids.rs module rather than per-type files. crates/enforcer-rules/src/registry.rs already consumes RuleId exclusively as its BTreeMap key and lookup parameter type.
why: The workpack was authored before this reconciliation landed and names a file path that was never created under that name; RuleId already satisfied nearly every Requirement Checklist item on arrival.
howToApply: Before creating a workpack-named file, grep for the type name across the crate first -- if a shared newtype module (ids.rs style) already exists and is wired into downstream consumers, extend it in place rather than duplicating or renaming.

statement: Added one test to crates/enforcer-domain/src/ids.rs: rule_id_required_at_a_registry_shaped_boundary_not_bare_string, mirroring the pre-existing hub_name_and_lane_id_are_not_interchangeable test's style. It builds a BTreeMap<RuleId, _> plus a &RuleId-typed lookup helper and documents (in comments, since no trybuild harness is vendored) that a bare String/&str key does not type-check against either. This was the one Requirement Checklist gap: TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md's a03 row explicitly names a 'compile-reject (bare String in a RuleId field)' proof that did not yet exist as a named test, even though the property itself (RuleId's private field + validating constructor) was already true.
why: Everything else in a03's Requirement Checklist and Acceptance And Proof sections (private field, parse-at-boundary ctor, serde round-trip, fail-closed malformed-id rejection, registry consumption via enforcer-rules::registry) was already present and unchanged; only the explicit named proof artifact was missing.
howToApply: When a proof-expectations row names a specific test shape (e.g. 'compile-reject') that the acceptance criteria already satisfy structurally, add a small test that documents/exercises the guarantee at the exact boundary named in the row (here: a registry-shaped map, since the row calls out ruleId<->registry parity) rather than re-deriving the type from scratch.

statement: cargo build --workspace from a clean worktree (post hard-reset to origin/rust-build) took ~14 minutes; the scoped cargo build -p enforcer-domain, cargo test -p enforcer-domain, and cargo clippy -p enforcer-domain --all-targets -- -D warnings gates each completed in well under 2 minutes once the workspace dependency graph was warm. All gates were clean with zero #[allow] added.
why: Useful baseline for other P0 domain lanes (a04/a05/a06) running concurrently on the same shared machine: the full workspace build is the expensive step; per-crate gates after that are fast.
howToApply: Run the full `cargo build --workspace` once early to warm the target dir, then rely on the fast per-crate gates for the actual pack verification loop.
